scope.indication: Moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis in adults

content.headline: After a TNF inhibitor, a different mechanism
content.lede: For your patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response to one or more TNF inhibitors, Tarnexa offers a once-daily oral option with a selective JAK1 mechanism.
content.claimText: In ESTUARY-1, 58% of patients receiving Tarnexa 15 mg once daily plus background csDMARD achieved ACR20 at week 24 vs 29% with placebo plus csDMARD (p<0.001). ACR50 was achieved by 34% vs 13%.
content.fairBalanceText: Tarnexa is indicated for adults with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response or intolerance to one or more TNF inhibitors. Boxed warning: serious infections, mortality, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events, thrombosis. See full Prescribing Information.
mslTalkingPoints: Primary endpoint ACR20 at week 24; secondary ACR50/70, DAS28-CRP, HAQ-DI
Background csDMARD required in ESTUARY-1; monotherapy data is ESTUARY-2 (REF-002)
Prespecified multi-TNF-IR subgroup is REF-005, do not extrapolate from this fragment
No head-to-head data vs any marketed agent; decline comparative questions

kolQuote.text: The question I get after a first TNF inhibitor fails is whether to cycle or switch mechanism. Data in the TNF-IR population is what lets me answer that for the patient in front of me.
kolQuote.attribution: Dr. Ines Okafor-Lindqvist, rheumatologist, Portland, ME (fictional)
